name: Placenta Accreta Spectrum Disorder

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Ultrasound and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Placenta Accreta Spectrum

criteria.description: Loss of the hypoechoic retroplacental clear zone on ultrasound
Presence of multiple irregular vascular lacunae within the placenta on Doppler imaging
Failure of placental separation during delivery with evidence of abnormal adherence to the myometrium
MRI evidence of placental invasion beyond the uterine serosa
Previous cesarean delivery or uterine surgery increasing suspicion

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Intraoperative evidence of abnormal placental adherence is required; diagnosis is supported by major ultrasound criteria and clinical history.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Prenatal diagnosis relies heavily on imaging; definitive diagnosis is often made intraoperatively.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Inability to manually separate placenta postpartum
Massive postpartum hemorrhage due to placental adherence
searchTerms: heavy bleeding after delivery due to placenta adherence
massive postpartum hemorrhage from placenta problems
excessive bleeding caused by retained placenta

common.symptomName: Antepartum vaginal bleeding in the third trimester
Abnormal placental lacunae detected on ultrasound
common.notes: Irregular vascular spaces within the placenta
searchTerms: unusual placental blood spaces on ultrasound

common.notes: May be present in some cases

common.symptomName: History of prior cesarean section or uterine surgery

occasional.notes: May occur due to placental abnormalities

searchTerms: irregular shape of uterus on scan
high AFP blood test in pregnancy

rare.symptomName: Ureteral obstruction due to placental invasion
searchTerms: urine flow obstruction due to placenta
blood in urine from bladder invasion
severe blood clotting problem after birth
widespread bleeding and clotting after delivery

laboratory: Decreased hemoglobin and hematocrit due to hemorrhage
imaging: Ultrasound showing loss of retroplacental clear zone and placental lacunae
MRI revealing placental invasion beyond uterine serosa
other: Intraoperative findings of placental adherence and inability to separate placenta
History of prior uterine surgery or cesarean section

distinguishingFeatures: Placenta previa involves placental location over cervical os without invasion
Usually presents with painless vaginal bleeding
Retained placenta is failure to deliver placenta but without abnormal invasion
No abnormal vascular lacunae on imaging

redFlags: Massive postpartum hemorrhage refractory to uterotonics
History of multiple cesarean sections with abnormal placental location
references: Jauniaux E, et al. Placenta accreta spectrum: pathophysiology and evidence-based clinical management. Am J Obstet Gynecol. 2018.
Silver RM. Placenta Accreta Spectrum. Obstet Gynecol. 2015.
